get.description: Connections to S3-compatible storage, by name. Secret keys are never returned.

put.description: Change a connection; leave out `secret_access_key` to keep the saved one.

post.description:
Ingest a CSV, TSV, JSON, JSONL or Parquet file, optionally gzipped: either upload `file` or give
a `source`. The format is detected from the file's content.

How often two or more columns give the same value in each row: several models' answers,
a model against labels someone already has, or any columns at all. With a `reference`, also
each column's accuracy against it. Every count comes with the filter for its rows, to use in a
scope's `filters`: to see them (`query`) or to ask about them again (`runs`).
Render a prompt template for a page of rows, with warnings and token estimates.

get.description:
Download the dataset as a CSV, JSONL or Parquet file, named after it. Nested values are JSON
text in CSV. A dataset still being made can't be exported until its run is done.

post.description: Write the dataset as CSV, JSONL or Parquet to a file on the server, or to S3.

Queue a run of every task with every model on the rows in the scope (all rows if none is
given). It makes a new dataset (`dataset_id`), created right away with every row; the answer
columns of the rows in scope fill in as the run works through them in the background: poll
`GET /v1/runs/{id}` for its progress. Answers already given are free: they come from the
response cache.

A task needs only its `template` and `type`; the result column and models default to ones that
suit the type (see `GET /v1/task-types`).

What `POST /v1/datasets/{id}/runs` with the same body would take and roughly cost, and why
it can't run as it is, if so. Nothing is asked.
Stop after the calls in flight. The chunk in progress is redone on resume, for free.

Continue a stopped or failed run, or a done one with failed answers: its failed answers are
asked again first, then it continues from its first unwritten chunk.

put.description: Check the key with OpenRouter and save it locally.

get.description: Models a job can use: decision models, then LLMs with structured outputs, each cheapest first.

The answer types a task can have (classify, extract, write), starting points for write tasks,
and the types an extracted field can have.
